Severe balance issues that directly effect campaign. You almost have to wait for a new balance to play certain levels. The Devs constantly keep re-balancing the civilizations and because they never get it right it just makes the game not fun. Some civs are just unplayable and it directly affects the difficulty of the campaigns which makes the levels also not fun. The spike in difficulty from easy to medium is absurd. Every update consists of a new balance but no new civs, levels, or editing tools. You need to download mods to obtain new levels. There is no level or scenario editor, It's extremely frustrating to see such a great game fall into such incredibly abysmal disorder. If you're looking for a good Medieval strategy game. Just get Stronghold: Crusader.

Devs: Please just make the civs functional and add new ones and add level editor. The campaign is not fun in its current state. I'm not interested in playing online with sweats who play for money. Please make this game accessiblely fun for singleplayer use. Thanks. Sincerely - someone' who's been playing since the early 2000s.

I don’t recommend Age of Empires 4 not because of the game itself, but because of the player base. A lot of them have this superiority complex and will belittle you if you don’t play exactly the way they do. It turns what could’ve been a fun, strategic experience into something stressful and draining. Instead of enjoying the game and learning at your own pace, you end up constantly feeling judged or pressured. It just kills the vibe completely.

Age of Empires IV is something very special. It's a game players have waited over 15 years for. It's for a good reason, too. How do you follow up on some of the best real-time strategy games of all time? Needless to say, Age of Empires IV has big shoes to fill, but if successful, it could lead to a new age for both the series and strategy games in general. I'm very happy to say that those shoes were too small for Age of Empires IV because it far exceeded my expectations and will delight longtime fans and newcomers alike with its incredibly fun campaign, creative and asymmetric civilizations, and outstanding presentation quality.

Simple to understand, hard to master. IV strikes a good balance between AOE II and AOE III. It lacks the asymmetry and diversity of strategy that III had, but that simplicity makes it more accessible. It does not require the intense micromanagement of II, but is much more macro focused. If you don't want the micro-nerdiness of Starcraft or AOE II and don't want the complexity of AOE III, but you do want a macro-focused, quick-to-action RTS, AOE IV is the game you're looking for.

I love RTS games and have been playing AOE II up till I found this on sale. Love it! Nice upgrade from playing AOE II for all these years. Keeping AOE II on my laptop when I travel as that is about all it can handle anyways.

It'd be a lot easier to recommend this game if it had proven RTS staples such as a REAL SCENARIO EDITOR, the ability to watch old replays (SC2 could do it 10 years ago), and community favorites such as CO OP CAMPAIGNS. As it stands there is not much to do in single player.

With that said this game has an extremely fun multiplayer component that I am personally enjoying a lot and seems to have a very bright future ahead with a large expansion coming in less than a month and seemingly the full support of Microsoft.

The modernization features such as more realistic and historically accurate graphics and civilizations, very strongly differentiated factions, and faster paced and more responsive gameplay as well as better path finding in comparison to earlier entries of the series, are deeply appreciated.

Please add more single player and co-op content and you'll pull in a lot of casuals as this is an easy recommendation for more hardcore RTS players.
A fun entry into the AoE series. Feels like an improved AoE3 plus bits of AoE and AoE 2 added.

while playing age of empires 2 my knight sword was not long enough to penetrate deep into Hymen cavern. But after playing Age of empires 4 anniversary edition I was able through meditation and leveling up, to increase the size of my knight sword and penetrate fully, the Hymen Cavern. My girlfriend watched excitedly as I passed through the hymen cavern and thrust my sword repeatedly into the cervical mountain. From there I was able to fight the final boss, the dark lord of Ovaria. It was carnage but the boss had been defeated. I removed my bloody sword and declared the battle over, until the next time.

Living up to expectations after 20yrs of AoE2 was never going to be easy, but Relic did an incredible job making a game that is super fun, looks great, and has tremendous replayability with the amazingly diverse lineup of playstyles. DON'T SKIP THE CAMPAIGNS! Tremendously well done with awesome history videos sprinkled in.

I've played AOE since the beginning and have been stuck on AOE2 pretty much since it came out. Never got into AOE3 though I would like to return to it at some point. I've only just begun playing this game but I'm falling in love with it. It has most of the elements from AOE2 that I've grown accustomed to and have come to expect, but adds many new elements that bring entirely new dimensions and variety into the game play, for instance trade posts, sheep herding, professional scouts, and more that I'm still discovering. So not a lot to say yet but I am loving it and will probably invest a good amount of time in attempting to become at least as comfortable and proficient as I was with AOE2

If you like RTS, you will like this, so many new civs and units to learn and the game gets exciting quite quickly, within 10 minutes you're usually being attacked.

Its not as good as Warcraft II, but its comparable with AOE2 and AOM - what I really like is, it can seem like you are dead, but you can come back and still win.

What I don't like is that people can win by building a wonder, or killing just 4 of your buildings, so sometimes you can die even when you're not aware you're being attacked.

I began playing this series in 1997 with AoE 1. Granted, I was five and didn't really know what I was doing, but that game was what got me into the strategy game series. I grew up on Age of Empires. AoE 2 and Mythology are the ones I probably played the most. AoE 3 was fun, but different. Although I was never very good at the games, I always enjoyed them.

This review has little substance (I also don't typically do reviews), but I just want to say this to those who played the old games in the series and are now deciding whether to buy this one: it's definitely worth it. The nostalgia is there, but the developers don't seem to take advantage of that or abuse it. Overall, it's been a fun experience.

My most played game on Steam. As a Dad I have very little time for gaming these days. I mostly play offline against AI opponents for a relaxing match or two when I have time. It's carefully designed historically and gameplay is fun, engaging, and rewarding. It's like 3D chess and can be as intellectually stimulating as you want it to be. Highly recommend this game to any who are interested in the genre.

This review only talks about the 1v1 ladder experience, which was most of what I played for 100+ hours.

Extremely steep learning curve for someone who hasn't played any other AOE games. Tons of civ variety, which is a good thing for veterans who want to learn to play many strategies, but makes it very difficult to learn how to react to your opponent.

Fights are difficult to judge who is winning. This is true when both sides a-move, or when they both micro. Population efficiency feels imbalanced. When games go long enough where both players are pop capped, whichever civ has the most pop-efficient unit (often who has the better knight) has a huge advantage.

Feudal fights have much less units and unit types, and population efficiency does not matter, so fights are much more enjoyable and microable imo. However, it's unreliable to push and end games in age 2 due to the strength of static defences, so you are often forced to play long games.

Very excited to see the game develop. Just know its a new game and balancing is going to be expected. graphics are not cutting edge but pacing and mechanics of the game tends towards competitive play. Looking for a competitive rts? AOE4 is a great choice.

Rose colored glasses aside, the game still missing features and seems more like an early release than a complete game. Updates are to roll out and open up these features. Multiplayer is still difficult to play consistently leading me to single player games most often.
